correctness.rationale: Classical 321 pattern avoidance equals full commutativity in type A, and right weak-order predecessors remain fully commutative. Stembridge's heap theorem makes each principal interval a distributive order-ideal lattice. For a finite meet-semilattice with these intervals, each element's global join-irreducible downset changes by exactly one coordinate on covers and has cardinality its rank, so Hamming distance equals rank(u)+rank(v)-2rank(u meet v) via descent-to-meet path. 321-avoidance partitions into two increasing subsequences, giving max inversion floor(n^2/4); full cross-inversion forces balanced rotated two-block T_q. Distinct T_p have disjoint simple-atom sets and meet e, so two highest ranks give parity-sharp diameters, handling n=1,2. Independent full BFS n<=6 checked every vertex distance and diameters 0,1,4,7,12,17. This finite check is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Fully commutative/distributive principal-interval facts are Stembridge's theorem, and their isometric embedding mechanism follows Birkhoff; neither is newly claimed. Inversion statistics for 321 avoiding permutations are prior work. The claimed specialized sharp diameter (n²-1)/2 odd, n²/2-1 even and its two-block witnesses were not found in the inspected primary material; originality is specifically the extremal graph result and proof of meet-zero pairing.
